_comment: Swing timings, in simulation ticks at 60 ticks per second.
A swing runs windup -> active -> recovery. Only the active window can hit
anything. Windup is the tell: it is what makes an attack dodgeable, and it
is the single number to reach for when an enemy feels unfair. Recovery is
the price of missing -- long recovery makes a whiff punishable.
reach is measured in pixels from the body's centre to the far edge of the
swing; a tile is 16. arc_degrees is the full width of the cone, so 100
means 50 degrees either side of where you are facing.
_hero_comment: Every class has four attacks, in slot order: light, neutral, heavy,
ultimate (see game/skills.py). The five below are the light attacks -- the
ones each class has always had, on no cooldown, and the only ones the
reference bot ever presses. Leaving them untouched is what keeps every
measured balance number in this project measuring the same thing.
One rule holds across all five and is tested: every *light* attack winds up
faster than every enemy attack. The player reacts to enemies; enemies do
not react to the player. That puts a ceiling of 15 ticks on the five below,
because the quickest enemy tell in the game is the rat's bite at 16.
The rule stops at the light slot on purpose. A heavy or an ultimate that
telegraphs for half a second is not unfair the way an enemy doing it would
be -- it is a commitment the player chose to spend, with a cooldown behind
it, and the length of the tell is what makes it weigh anything.
Within that ceiling the classes are separated by the shape of the swing, not
by a damage-per-second number: how long you are committed, how much ground
the swing covers, and whether you have to be next to the thing at all.

greatsword.name: Greatsword
_comment: The Knight. Longest reach and widest arc of any hero weapon, and the only
one that reliably hits two things at once -- but a 30-tick cycle means a
whiff is half a second of standing still, which is a long time with three
grunts on you. Slow enough to be a decision, fast enough to still be a
hero weapon.

dagger.name: Dagger
_comment: The Rogue. A twelve-tick cycle -- the fastest thing in the game by a wide
margin. Almost no commitment, so a whiff costs nothing, but the narrow arc
and short reach mean you have to be genuinely in the right place, and the
low knockback does not buy you the space back afterwards.

shortbow.name: Shortbow
_comment: The Archer. Faster in the air than the enemy archer's arrow (2.7), which
is the whole difference between shooting and being shot at: yours lands
where you aimed it, theirs can be walked out of.
Note what a projectile costs. reach is 0, so nothing about being next to
an enemy helps, and a shot spends itself on the first body or wall it
meets -- a pillared arena that protects you from archers protects them
from you too.

arcane_bolt.name: Arcane Bolt
_comment: The Magician. The hardest single hit of any light attack, on the longest
light commitment -- 29 ticks, and 12 of them before the bolt exists.
Standing still for that long is the cost of the damage.
The 12-tick windup is the binding number for the whole rule above: the
rat's bite is 16, so there are four ticks of room and no more. Any slower
and a rat would be the faster tell, which would invert the rule the whole
fight rests on.
*** THE TWO PROJECTILE NUMBERS ARE WHAT CLOSED THE MAGICIAN XFAILS. ***
speed 3.4 -> 4.0 and radius 3.5 -> 4.5. Everything else here is what it
always was, and deliberately: damage and commitment ARE the class, and
four attempts at tuning them are recorded as failures in
tests/test_playthrough.py.
The bolt was missing. At 3.4 a bolt crossing the 120px the ranged policy
holds is 35 ticks in the air; a grunt walks 1.05px per tick, so it has
moved 37px -- four body widths -- by the time the bolt arrives, and
nothing in this game leads a target. Measured: the Magician landed 6.1-8.1
damage per shot against the Archer's 5.5-6.9 off a bolt worth 15 against
an arrow worth 9, which is a hit rate near half. It fired 37-42 times a
stage to deal 196 damage worth of kills and took 105+ doing it.
At 4.0/4.5 the same fight is 19-35 shots at 8.6-13.1 landed each, and the
damage taken roughly halves. Nothing about how hard the bolt hits or how
long you stand still for it changed -- only whether it arrives.
Both numbers, not one. Speed alone leaves stage 12 at 10/12; radius alone
leaves the run bracket at 2/3. Together the class goes 228/240 -> 240/240
on the base grid and 1/6 -> 6/6 on runs. The pair sits on a plateau, not
a spike: every combination from 4.5/4.0 up scores the same, and the edge
below it (4.0/3.8) drops back to 70/72. Room to tune, in one direction.
The shortbow is still the faster projectile at 4.2, and that ordering is
deliberate -- an arrow outrunning a bolt is the Archer's half of the
difference between the two ranged classes. 4.0 is the largest value that
keeps it.

censer.name: Censer
_comment: The Priest. Swung on a chain, so the arc is nearly a half-circle -- the
answer to being surrounded, which is the situation the Priest's middling
speed keeps walking into. Heavy knockback for the damage: it buys space
rather than killing things, which is the class in one number.

_skill_comment: The other three slots, five classes' worth. cooldown is in ticks and is
counted from the swing starting, so it is the gap between one use and the
next rather than a pause tacked onto the end of the recovery.
What each slot is for:
neutral   -- answers the situation the class's light attack is worst in.
Always does less damage than the light attack; what it buys
is position, or reach, or a crowd off you. ~3 seconds.
heavy     -- roughly double the light attack in damage and in commitment.
~5 seconds.
ultimate  -- the largest payoff the class has, once or twice a stage.
25-30 seconds.
**These are a first pass and they have not been measured.** Every other
number in this project was arrived at by running the campaign and reading
the result, and several were reverted when measurement contradicted them.
These were not, because the reference bot plays light-only by design and
therefore cannot see them. What is pinned by test is the *relationships*
-- neutral below light, heavy above it, cooldowns ascending -- not the
values. Treat them as a starting shape.
None of them dashes. charge_speed works perfectly well on a hero attack
and is left for later rather than ruled out: a lunging skill and the dodge
would want designing against each other, which is more than this pass is.

knight_bash.name: Shield Bash
_comment: The Knight's problem is that a 30-tick greatsword cycle is a long time
with three things on you, and the class is too slow to walk out of it.
This does almost no damage and shoves everything in front of you nearly
twice as far as the greatsword does, in a third of the commitment.

knight_onslaught.name: Onslaught
_comment: The whole circle, further than the Effigy's swing, and the hardest
knockback in the game. Seventy-four ticks of commitment for it -- longer
than any enemy attack -- so it is thrown into a crowd that has already
committed, not into one that is still deciding.

rogue_knife.name: Thrown Knife
_comment: The one thing a 20-pixel dagger cannot do is touch something that is not
already next to you. The fastest projectile in the game and the smallest,
on the shortest cooldown -- it is a way to start a fight or finish a rat,
not a way to fight at range.

rogue_impale.name: Impale
_comment: A 40-degree arc, the narrowest attack in the game. The Rogue's heavy is
the only one that can miss a body standing right in front of you, which
is the class: everything it does asks whether you are in exactly the
right place.

rogue_flurry.name: Flurry
_comment: Fourteen ticks of open hitbox across most of a circle. A swing hits each
body once, so the long active window is not extra damage -- it is a net
that catches whatever walks into it while it is out.

archer_kick.name: Kick
_comment: The Archer's stated weakness, answered directly: a shortbow has reach 0,
so a rat standing on you is a class that has stopped working. This is the
only melee attack a ranged class has and it is not there to kill anything
-- it is there to buy back the distance the whole class depends on.

archer_piercer.name: Piercer
archer_piercer._comment: The fastest thing in the air in the game, and it still stops on the first body.

archer_rain.name: Rain
_comment: The Warden's volley, pointed the other way. Five shots at 11 is more than
any single hit a class has, but only against a line of things -- against
one enemy four of the arrows are gone.

magician_ward.name: Ward
_comment: Three damage and the second-hardest shove in the game, all the way round,
in 26 ticks. The Magician's bolt is a 29-tick commitment on a body that
cannot afford to be interrupted, so what the class actually needs is not
more damage -- it is the room to spend that commitment.

magician_lance.name: Arcane Lance
_comment: The hardest single hit in the game and the largest projectile, moving
slower than the bolt it is a bigger version of. Fifty-three ticks of
commitment: this is the shot you take at something that has already
started its own attack.

magician_nova.name: Nova
magician_nova._comment: Seven bolts across eighty degrees. A room-clearer, aimed at a room.

priest_brand.name: Brand
_comment: The Priest is the only class with no answer at all to something across
the room -- a censer reaches 26 pixels and that is the whole kit. This is
a poke, not a bow: six damage every three seconds.

priest_consecrate.name: Consecrate
_comment: Nearly the whole circle at 26 damage, with knockback second only to the
Knight's ultimate. The Priest's answer to being surrounded is the censer
at a small scale and this at a large one -- the class is defined by not
having to leave.

_enemy_comment: Enemy attacks. Every windup here is longer than every hero *light* attack,
and a test enforces it. An enemy that strikes faster than you can start a
swing is not difficult, it is unfair. Hero heavies and ultimates are exempt

bite.name: Bite
_comment: The rat. The shortest tell in the game and the smallest hit -- one is
barely worth reacting to, which is the point: they arrive in numbers, and
the threat is arithmetic rather than any single bite. Still 16 ticks, so
the rule that enemies are slower to start than the hero survives even
against the Magician's 14.

gore.name: Gore
_comment: The active window is long because it stays open for the whole dash.
charge_speed belongs to the attack rather than to the creature: a body
with several attacks must only dash on the one that is a charge.

maul.name: Maul
_comment: The brute. Hits harder than anything short of a boss and telegraphs for
over half a second, so it is only ever a threat when something else has
already taken your attention. A brute alone is free damage; a brute behind
a wall of rats is what the second act is about.

hex_bolt.name: Hex
_comment: The mage. Slower and fatter than an arrow, and it hurts more. Slow enough
to walk out of once you have seen it, which makes it a punishment for
standing still rather than for being at range -- the same question the
archer asks, at a volume you cannot ignore.

_boss_comment: Boss attacks, three per boss and positional: the brain in game/ai.py reads
weapons[0] as the sweep, weapons[1] as the charge and weapons[2] as the
ranged attack. Declare them in any other order and the boss will telegraph
one attack and land another. A test enforces the ordering.
Each answers a different position, so a boss fight is about where you stand
rather than how fast you click:
sweep  -- punishes standing next to it
crush  -- punishes standing in a line with it
volley -- punishes standing still at range
All of them telegraph longer than anything else in the game. A boss that is
hard because it is fast is just an unfair grunt; these should be hard
because they are always asking you to be somewhere else.

boss_sweep.name: Sweep
boss_sweep._comment: Nearly all the way round, so backing off beats circling.

boss_crush.name: Crush
boss_crush._comment: The longest tell in the first act, and the hardest hit. Sidestep it.

boss_volley.name: Volley
boss_volley._comment: A fan, not a bullet -- you go around it rather than sidestep it.

_houndmaster_comment: Act II. The Warden taught you to read a long tell; this one asks whether
you can still do it in a hurry. Every timing is shorter and every number is
smaller -- the same three questions, asked faster.

hound_lunge.name: Lunge
hound_lunge._comment: Faster than the Warden's crush and shorter to read. Commit early.

hound_spray.name: Spray
_comment: Tight and fast rather than wide and slow. The Warden's volley is walked
around; this one is put a pillar in front of.

_effigy_comment: Act III. The opposite reading of the same fight: everything is slower than
the Warden and everything is bigger. Nothing here is hard to see coming and

effigy_swing.name: Swing
effigy_swing._comment: Past a half-circle and longer than a pillar is wide. Leave.

effigy_topple.name: Topple
_comment: The longest tell in the game -- three quarters of a second of warning --
and the hardest hit outside the final fight. Being caught by this is not
a reaction failure, it is a positioning one.

effigy_embers.name: Embers
effigy_embers._comment: Slow and everywhere. Cover, not footwork.

_sovereign_comment: Act IV. Nothing new to learn -- the same three questions the Warden asked
on stage five, with none of the room. It is the last fight in the game and
it is allowed to be the hardest.

sovereign_lance.name: Lance
_comment: Slightly lighter than the Warden's crush, fifteen stages later, on a
body that moves faster and has more health behind it. The Sovereign is
not the hardest-hitting thing in the game and was never meant to be:
its rain is nine shots to the Warden's five, which is half again the
damage at range, and its reach and speed are greater everywhere else.
Measured: at 17 it took the final stage to 22 wins in 24, which is a
capstone that sometimes just kills you.

sovereign_rain.name: Rain
_comment: Nine shots across most of a half-circle. There is no standing at range
against this one -- the answer is a pillar or being close enough that the
fan has not opened yet, and being close is what the arc is for.

_advanced_comment: The promoted classes' heavy and ultimate slots -- two attacks each, ten
classes, twenty weapons. An advanced class inherits its base's light and
neutral by id, so those two slots are unchanged and the class still opens a
fight the way the one it grew out of did.
**These are a first pass and nothing measures them**, exactly as with the
fifteen above and for a worse reason: the reference bot plays light-only
*and* never promotes, so it cannot see these attacks at all. What is pinned
by test is the same set of relationships every class obeys -- heavy above
light, ultimate payload above heavy, cooldowns ascending. Treat every number
here as a starting shape.
They were drafted for one specific fight, and it shows. Promotion used to
happen on the way into the final stage, so the Sovereign was the only enemy
any of these would ever meet: a 210-degree arc up close, a committed lance
at mid range, nine shots from far. Each pair is one branch that kills it
faster and one that survives it longer, and that framing is why every one
of these twenty is a burst rather than anything sustained.
They now see twenty stages and four bosses. Nothing here has been re-drafted
for that, and it is the most obvious place to look for a number that feels
wrong -- an ultimate on a 1500-tick cooldown is a once-a-stage decision in a
campaign, where against a single boss it was the whole plan.
What keeps that from being urgent: acts V-VIII are tuned against the light
attack these classes inherit, not against any of the twenty below. A number
here being generous makes a stage easier than the grid says; it cannot make
one unwinnable.
None of them dashes, for the same reason none of the base skills do.

dark_knight_ruin.name: Ruin
dark_knight_ruin._comment: Cleave with the guard dropped: six more damage for six more ticks.

dark_knight_black_tide.name: Black Tide
_comment: The hardest hit in the game, behind the longest commitment in the game --
82 ticks, nearly a second and a half. Thrown at something already swinging,
never at something deciding.

holy_knight_bulwark.name: Bulwark
_comment: Six less damage than the Cleave it replaces and half again the shove,
across an arc wide enough that backing off beats circling -- the Sovereign's
own Arc, answered in kind.

holy_knight_sanctuary.name: Sanctuary
_comment: The hardest knockback in the game and twelve ticks of open hitbox. Not a
kill -- a reset. Everything touching you is somewhere else afterwards.

assassin_eviscerate.name: Eviscerate
_comment: The narrowest attack in the game, narrower than the Impale it replaces.
Nine more damage for four more ticks, and it will miss a body standing
slightly to one side of where you are looking.

assassin_deathmark.name: Deathmark
_comment: Nearly twice the Flurry's damage into a fiftieth of its arc. The Rogue's
ultimate stops being a net and becomes a single answer to a single body,
which is the whole difference between the two branches.

shadow_rogue_shadowstep.name: Shadowstep
_comment: Twenty-six ticks: the fastest heavy in the game, across a half-circle. One
more damage than the Impale for half the commitment and four times the arc
-- the Rogue's answer to being surrounded rather than to being precise.

shadow_rogue_umbral_veil.name: Umbral Veil
_comment: Sixteen ticks of open hitbox, the longest in the game. A swing hits each
body once, so that window is not extra damage -- it is a wider net than
the Flurry's, held open longer.

hunter_deadeye.name: Deadeye
_comment: The fastest thing in the air in the game at 6.0, and the longest-lived.
Six more damage than the Piercer on a shorter windup -- and it still stops
on the first body, because nothing in this game pierces.

hunter_hunt.name: Hunt
_comment: The Rain, tightened. Five shots across thirty degrees instead of fifty, so
against one large body most of them land -- which is the difference between
an ultimate for a crowd and an ultimate for a boss.

magic_archer_runeshot.name: Runeshot
_comment: The fattest projectile in the game -- wider than the Magician's Lance --
and slower than the Piercer it replaces. Two damage less, and much harder
to miss with.

magic_archer_starfall.name: Starfall
_comment: Nine shots across a hundred degrees: the Sovereign's own Rain, pointed the
other way, and the largest total payload of any hero attack. Against one
body most of it misses -- this is aimed at a room.

sage_aegis.name: Aegis
_comment: The whole circle, hard enough to matter and heavy enough to clear a path.
The Magician's real problem is that a 29-tick bolt is a long time to be
uninterrupted; the Lance answers it with more damage and this answers it
with room.
Drafted at 8 damage as a pure control tool and rejected by test: a heavy
must out-damage its class's light attack, and the Magician's is the
hardest in the game at 15. The rule was right -- at 8 this was a slower
Ward, which the Sage already has in the neutral slot.

sage_convergence.name: Convergence
_comment: The Nova, narrowed from eighty degrees to forty. Same seven bolts, half
the spread, so it is a wall walked into rather than a spray walked around.

wizard_annihilate.name: Annihilate
_comment: The hardest single projectile in the game and the slowest, on a 61-tick
commitment. Eight more damage than the Lance for eight more ticks, and it
travels slowly enough that a moving target will not be there.

wizard_cataclysm.name: Cataclysm
wizard_cataclysm._comment: The Nova with four more damage a bolt, on the longest cooldown in the game.

battle_priest_crusade.name: Crusade
_comment: Four more damage than the Smite and four ticks quicker, over a narrower
arc. The Priest stops buying space and starts spending it.

battle_priest_zealot.name: Zealot
battle_priest_zealot._comment: Four more damage than Consecrate across two thirds of its arc. Closer in, harder.

holy_priest_benediction.name: Benediction
_comment: Four less damage than the Smite, a much wider arc and half again the
shove. The censer at a larger scale, which is what the class already was.

holy_priest_absolution.name: Absolution
_comment: The full circle where Consecrate stops thirty degrees short, and knockback
second only to the Holy Knight's. Nothing is standing next to you when it
ends.

_acts_v_to_viii_comment: Everything below is fought only after the fork, by a hero that has just
replaced two of its four attacks. That is the one thing that makes these
numbers different in kind from the four acts above: the hero's output
It moved less than it looks, though, and the amount is worth knowing before
changing anything here. An advanced class keeps the light attack it was
promoted with -- the same greatsword, the same shortbow -- and the light is
the attack a fight is mostly made of. What promotion buys is a heavy and an
ultimate, which are a few presses a stage, plus a health number that moves
either way. So acts V-VIII are tuned as though the hero swings what it
always swung, and the new kit is upside rather than a requirement.
The windups stay above twelve ticks throughout, which is the reference
bot's reaction time -- an attack that opens and lands inside that window is
not a tell, it is a tax, and it cannot be answered by any policy.

rend.name: Rend
_comment: The revenant. Sits between the claw and the maul on every dial, which is
the point of it: a grunt you cannot afford to leave and a brute you cannot
walk away from. The windup is two ticks longer than a claw and the reach
two pixels further, so it out-trades a grunt without ever reading like a
different question.

demon_claw.name: Rake
_comment: The demon, and deliberately the least interesting thing about it. A rend
with a point knocked off the damage and two ticks added to the tell.
The demon's question is the flanking approach, not the hit at the end of
it -- so the hit is drafted to be answerable by everything the player
already knows. Giving a new brain a new weapon as well would make it two
new things at once and leave nobody able to say which of them was the
part that felt wrong.
Sits comfortably clear of the binding constraint: the slowest class light
attack is the Magician's 12-tick bolt, and every enemy tell in the game
has to be longer than that.

lunge.name: Lunge
_comment: The stalker. A gore with six ticks shaved off the tell and a longer
commitment behind it -- 26 against the reference bot's twelve-tick
reaction leaves fourteen ticks to move, where the charger leaves twenty.
That margin is the whole enemy, and it is the reason this is a charger
rather than another chaser: the promoted kit is built on commitment, and
the heavy and the ultimate it just gained are the longest commitments the
hero has ever had. Something has to punish spending one at the wrong
moment, or the new attacks are free.

_new_boss_comment: Four more, one per act, in the same positional order every boss uses:
sweep close, charge at mid, projectile from far. See the boss comment in
entities.json -- declaring them in any other order makes a boss telegraph
one attack and land another, and a test catches it.
None of them is dramatically tankier than the Sovereign, and that is a
measurement rather than a preference: boss health buys fight *length* and
little else, and both act III and act IV bosses were drafted far heavier
and were unwinnable on every seed. What separates these four is cadence,
reach and how much of the arena each one denies.

herald_peal.name: Peal
_comment: The Herald is the first fight after the fork and it is deliberately the
Houndmaster's question again -- everything short, everything quick -- so
that the first thing a promoted class meets is a pattern it already
knows. What is new is that it asks all three at a range the Warden never
reached to.

gaoler_chain.name: Chain
_comment: The longest reach in the game, on the longest tell of the four. Backing
out of it is not possible from inside; the answer is to already be
somewhere else when it opens.

gaoler_shackles.name: Shackles
_comment: Slow, fat and only six of them. The Gaoler's ranged attack is the one you
walk out of; the reason to respect it is where walking out of it puts
you, which is usually inside the chain.

choir_chorus.name: Chorus
_comment: Eleven shots across most of a half-circle, and the lightest hit of any
boss projectile -- the Choir is arithmetic rather than any single shot.
It is also the weakest of the four up close, on purpose: this is the one
fight where closing the distance is the answer, and its arena is built
with the pillars to make that survivable.

hollow_dirge.name: Dirge
_comment: The last fight, and nothing in it is new. Ten shots where the Sovereign
had nine, a shade more reach on the arc, a shade more speed on the ruin.
That is the intent: the fortieth stage should be the thing you have spent
the run learning to read, at the top of every dial at once, rather than a
final exam on a moveset introduced on the final stage.

regent_edict.name: Edict
_comment: The shortest recovery any boss sweep has, and the only dial on this
fight that is a record. Everything else about the Regent is ordinary --
less reach than the Hollow Arc, less damage than the Sovereign's -- and
that is the point: what it costs you is that the gap after a swing is
twenty-two ticks instead of twenty-six, so the room it gives back is
not enough to leave in.
The windup is left at twenty-six, matching the Herald and the Choir. A
shorter tell would make the fight about reaction, and reaction is
measured elsewhere and found not to be what decides a run.

regent_seal.name: Seal
_comment: The fastest charge in the game and the longest-lived, thrown from a
charge_range of 250 rather than the Hollow King's 235. Together those
three numbers are the whole fight: there is no distance at which this
one is not already coming.

regent_writ.name: Writ
_comment: Six shots in a 70-degree cone -- the smallest volley of any boss past
the fork, deliberately. A wide fan is a reason to hold a pillar, and
holding a pillar is exactly the rest this fight is built to refuse. It
is here so that standing still at range is not free, and for nothing
else.

unmade_sunder.name: Sunder
_comment: The longest reach on any sweep, two past the Gaoler's chain, across a
235-degree arc. Being beside it is not being out of it.
Windup thirty and recovery thirty: slower than the Regent's cadence by
a third. The last two bosses are the same fight asked from opposite
ends -- one that never lets you stop, and one that gives you the room
and makes every piece of it dangerous.

unmade_collapse.name: Collapse
_comment: The hardest single hit in the game, behind the longest tell of any boss
charge, at the slowest crossing speed of any of them. Thirty-six ticks
is a third of a second and is meant to be readable from anywhere in the
room -- the damage is the punishment for not answering it, not for
failing to see it.
**3.5 rather than the 4.0 it was drafted at, and this one dial was the
whole fight for one class.** The Dark Knight cleared stage 50 on 1 seed
in 6 while the other nine advanced classes cleared it 6/6, and it died
every time with the boss around fifty health from dead -- close, which
is what made it look like a health problem. It was not: 220 down to 200
bought one seed and 4.0 down to 3.5 bought all six, with the health
left where it was.
The reason is the class rather than the number. The Dark Knight is the
fastest body in the game on the least health of the knight branches, so
it fights this one from inside the sweep, and a charge that crosses that
distance faster than it can leave is not a telegraph, it is a tax. Every
slower class was already answering it.
Damage stayed at 18. A charge that hits for less is a smaller mistake;
a charge that arrives slower is a mistake you are allowed to see coming,
and only one of those is what the fight is supposed to be about.

unmade_silence.name: Silence
_comment: Twelve shots across 140 degrees, the widest fan in the game -- the
Choir's idea on a body that cannot be waited out. The Choir is the
least healthy boss because closing it is the fight; this one has the
most health of anything, so closing it is only the first half.
Slow shots on purpose, at 2.8. A wide fan of fast projectiles has one
answer and it is a wall; a wide fan of slow ones can be walked out of,
which is the difference between a fight and a tax.
